Plain_English_Explanation: The customer initiated or interacted with the case digitally through the bank's online web/mobile portal.
Service Level Agreement (SLA) urgency tier demanding immediate escalation and fast-tracking.
Service Level Agreement (SLA) urgency tier following standard operational queues.
Mandatory identity verification process to confirm the client's legal identity, address, and background.
Global compliance screening check to ensure the client is not a high-risk political figure.
Global compliance screening check to ensure the client is not on international trade or terrorism sanction lists.
The ratio of the loan amount compared to the appraised value of the collateral. Higher LTV increases credit risk.
A governing body of senior risk officers required to review and approve loans exceeding standard underwriting authority matrices. Not related to credit cards.
The percentage of a client's monthly gross income that goes toward paying debts. High DTI signals repayment stress.
The approval tier that limits how much a signer can authorize. Case comments such as 'LOA Level 3' name the tier of the approving officer.
The bank's primary backend central ledger and transaction processing software where final balances and account statuses are updated.
Fully automated transaction processing from start to finish without requiring manual human intervention.
The natural person(s) who ultimately own or control a corporate entity or SME client during commercial onboarding.
A metric measuring a company's available cash flow to pay current debt obligations. A ratio above 1.0 indicates positive cash flow coverage.

Full_Form: Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization
Plain_English_Explanation: A core indicator of a company's overall financial profitability and operational performance.
The standardized electronic system used to transfer securities and assets between different brokerages or financial institutions.
Standardized consumer credit scoring model used to evaluate individual creditworthiness.
Protocol providing an additional layer of authentication for online credit card transactions to prevent fraud.
A client request to raise the maximum borrowing threshold on their existing revolving credit card line.
Standard US tax document used to verify employee wage earnings.
Standard US tax document used to verify independent contractor or self-employed earnings.
Checks that a client's funds and activity are not linked to money laundering or other financial crime.
The bank staff member who manages the client relationship and often submits requests on the client's behalf.
A transaction made in person at a merchant's terminal, such as a card swipe or tap at a store.
An automated rule ID in the bank's decision engine. The case was approved automatically under this rule, with no manual review.
A reversal of a card payment, requested through the card network when a customer disputes a transaction and the merchant must justify it.
A temporary credit given to the customer while a disputed transaction is investigated. It can be reversed if the dispute is denied.
A request for the customer's credit report and score from a credit bureau, used in credit decisions.
A formal letter sent when credit is declined or limited. It must state the reasons, and the customer has the right to know them.
A signed statement from a donor confirming that money used for a home purchase is a gift, not a loan.
A review of public property records to confirm the legal owner of a property and whether it has any claims or liens against it.
An independent estimate of a property's market value. It is the value used to calculate LTV.
A court document confirming that a named executor has authority to manage an estate of a deceased person.
The tax number that identifies a business or individual to tax authorities. It is checked during commercial onboarding.
An approval that takes effect only after the listed conditions, such as extra collateral or missing documents, are met.
The share of a credit card's limit currently in use. High utilization can signal financial stress and lowers credit scores.
A set of rules that lets one software system send data to another, such as updating the core banking system automatically.
A text message sent to the customer's mobile phone, used here for confirmations and notifications.
A business credit line used to fund day-to-day operating costs such as payroll, inventory, and bills.
A document from an employer showing a worker's pay for a period. Underwriters compare it with other income records to verify earnings.
A document signed in front of a licensed notary public, who confirms the signer's identity. Used for legal and estate paperwork.
An official government record of a person's death. It is required before an estate account can be opened or managed.
A legally binding signature captured digitally, such as on a screen, instead of on paper.
The specialist who reviews trust and estate accounts, including the authority of executors and beneficiaries.
A person approved to act on an account, such as signing transactions or instructions for it.
A check that the securities listed in a transfer request match the holdings at the sending institution.
The merchant's formal response to a card dispute, with evidence that the transaction was valid.
An asset pledged to secure a loan. The lender can claim it if the borrower does not repay.
The review of a credit request to judge risk and decide whether to approve it, and on what terms.
A small or medium-sized business customer. Commercial cases for SMEs follow business-banking checks, such as identifying the owners.
An electronic transfer of funds from one bank account to another, usually settled the same day.

Replacing an existing home loan with a new one, usually to obtain a lower rate or different terms. The new loan is underwritten like a new mortgage, so the property's appraisal, LTV, and income checks apply.
